title: Handover Velocity: Operator Succession & Rapid Bridge Acceleration Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a compact, auditable process for accelerating handovers (handover velocity) when an incident requires quick succession of responders, bridge escalation, or takeover from shadow->solo oncall. It is optimized for LLM-serving incidents (latency surges, KV cache evictions, throttling) but applies broadly to multi-service degradations. The goal: reduce time-to-stable while preserving evidence collection and clear customer comms.

Scope
-----
- Applies to: primary oncall, secondary pager, bridge operator, service steward, incident commander (IC).
- Not covered: full legal/regulatory disclosure (see security-and-compliance policies).

Quick definitions
-----------------
- Handover Velocity: time from decision to handoff to the new operator actively owning the bridge (~target: <= 5 minutes for Tier 1 SEVs).
- Bridge Acceleration: set of pre-authorized actions to reduce friction during handover (automated credentials swap, pre-bound dashboards).
- Shadow-to-Solo: structured progression for new responders to reach independent responder competency.

Roles & Roster (ownership)
--------------------------
- Primary Oncall: first responder, owns initial TTR (time-to-respond) and triage.
- Secondary Pager: backup for escalations and escalation-authorized actions.
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge and external comms.
- Service Steward: long-lived owner of the affected service; coordinates patching and post-incident work.
- IC: invoked for multi-service or customer-impacting incidents (Severity >= 2).

Handover Velocity policy (targeted SLOs)
----------------------------------------
| Metric | Target | Escalation trigger | Notes |
|-------|--------|--------------------|-------|
| Acknowledge window | <= 2m | >2m escalate to secondary | measured by PagerDuty ack time |
| Handover time (shadow->solo) | <= 5m (Tier 1) | >5m escalate to IC | includes context transfer and active cursor on bridge |
| Evidence snapshot time | <= 10m | >10m create forensic ticket | full set of metrics/logs retained |

Prerequisites (automation & access)
----------------------------------
- Bridge room template in Slack/MS Teams: /ops/bridges/templates/fast-handover.
- Pre-bound dashboards: Grafana links: service-latency, token-e2e, kv-cache-miss-rate.
- One-click credential swap: Kubernetes serviceaccount impersonation and temporary SSH jump role configured per-service.
- Verified runbook snippet for each critical path (see Runbook Invocation).

Handover checklist (5-minute run)
--------------------------------
1) Declare handover intent in bridge: "Handover requested: <reason>" and set expected ETA.
2) Create Handover note (bridge channel): include timeline, actions tried, hypothesis, and observed metrics.
3) Secondary/Successor: confirm readback of key facts (SLOs affected, affected regions, current mitigation).
4) Share ephemeral access token or use pre-authorized session link.
5) Successor runs first confirmation step from runbook (see example below).
6) If successor cannot confirm within 5 minutes, IC invoked and bridge shifted to IC-led mode.

Shadow-to-Solo progression (competency ladder)
---------------------------------------------
- Stage 0: Observes 3 full incidents (shadow).
- Stage 1: Paired handover with active micro-responsibilities (e.g., run diagnostics) x5 incidents.
- Stage 2: Solo on low-risk incidents with mentor review (x10 incidents).
- Stage 3: Full solo for Tier 1 incidents; authorized to perform hotfixes and customer notices.

Bridge Acceleration patterns (authorized quick-actions)
----------------------------------------------------
- Pre-approve "soft rollback" for non-stateful model variants (owner: Service Steward).
- Allowed quick-action: scale up dedicated capacity pool by +25% for 15 minutes (automated Terraform plan + apply token).
- Allowed quick-action: enable model-variant fallback (R0 -> R1) via routing control plane toggle.

Runbook invocation (example: KV cache eviction causing latency spike)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose: rapidly stabilize read-latency and rehydrate cache where applicable.
Steps:
1) Assess impact: check KV miss-rate, tail latency, and error rate. Grafana panels: kv-miss-rate (5m), p95-latency (1m).
2) Activate degraded-mode routing: set route policy to prefer regional cached replicas (CLI):
   - CLI snippet:
     redwoodctl routing set-policy --service model-serve --policy degraded-prefer-cache --duration 15m
3) If miss-rate > 10% and p95 > 750ms, scale read pool
   - k8s: kubectl scale deployment/model-reader --replicas=8 -n model-serving
4) Rehydrate hotset: run cache-warm job (namespace: infra-tools):
   - kubectl apply -f jobs/cache-rehydrate-job.yaml -n infra-tools
5) Monitor: check kv-cache-hit-rate > 85% and p95 < 400ms. If not, proceed to model-variant fallback.
6) Communicate: update bridge with status template (see Customer Status Templates).

Customer status templates (for status page and bridge)
----------------------------------------------------
Use the following templates for quick, consistent comms. Replace bracketed fields.

Status page short blurb (public):
"We are investigating increased latency affecting model responses in [region]. Our team has identified issues with KV cache misses; mitigations are in progress and customer impact is limited to a subset of traffic. We will post updates every 15 minutes until resolved."

Customer-facing update (email/support):
Subject: Incident update: Increased inference latency in [region]
Body:
- What happened: We detected increased latency for model responses for requests routed to [region].
- Impact: Some requests may return slower responses (p95 up to [value]ms). No data loss reported.
- Mitigations: We've applied routing changes and cache rehydration jobs; scaling enabled.
- Next update: [time + 15min].

Bridge internal status line (bridge channel):
"Incident [INC-YYYY] | Step 3/6 | In-progress: cache rehydrate; scale applied; monitoring target p95<400ms"

Game day scenarios (fast-handover drills)
----------------------------------------
- Scenario A: KV cache silent evaporation in single region (objective: handover time <= 5m, restore p95 < 400ms within 20m).
- Scenario B: Noisy neighbor GPU starvation causing increased queuing (objective: scale or reroute within 10m).
- Scenario C: Model quality regression after canary rollout (objective: rollback via routing fallback within 7m).

Each game day includes: pre-brief, role assignments, 30-min active incident, 30-min retro focusing on handover timing and friction points. Use markers: T0 (alert), T1 (bridge open), T2 (handover), T_end (stable).

Post-incident artifacts & postmortem fast-track
----------------------------------------------
Required deliverables within 72 hours:
- Short chronology (timeline) with timestamps (T0 .. T_end).
- Evidence bundle: Grafana snapshots, key logs (30min before/after), pager trace.
- Action items with owners and due dates.
- Handover review: was handover velocity met? If not, list blockers and remediation.

Mini-RCA template (single paragraph):
- Root cause: [one-sentence root cause].
- Contributing factors: [bullets].
- Immediate fix: [what was done].
- Long-term corrective actions: [3 actions, owners, ETA].

Operational metrics to track (weekly cadence)
--------------------------------------------
- Average handover velocity for Tier 1 incidents (goal <= 5m).
- Percentage of successful shadow->solo promotions per quarter.
- Average time-to-stable (p95) for KV incidents.
- Game day pass rate (able to meet targets).

Appendix: quick links, CLI, and monitoring queries
-------------------------------------------------
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/service-latency
- Pager rules: PagerDuty -> Team: model-serving-oncall
- redwoodctl diagnostics command (light weight snapshot):
  redwoodctl diagnostics snapshot --service model-serve --window 5m --out /tmp/diag-$(date +%s).tar.gz

- Sample monitoring query (PromQL):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_requests_total[1m])) * 100

Governance & continuous improvement
----------------------------------
- After each incident where Handover Velocity > 5m, run a micro-retro focused on friction removal and automation candidates.
- Quarterly review of shadow-to-solo promotions maintained by eng-sre; training quota: each responder must shadow >=3 incidents per quarter.

Contact and ownership
---------------------
- Document owner: Maya Chen (model-serving SRE).
- Operational steward: Diego Alvarez.
- Escalation: PagerDuty schedule (see team rota).
